questions.text: TAT in insurance claims processing stands for:
questions.explanation: TAT stands for TURNAROUND TIME. It is the specific time period within which the insurance company must complete loss assessment, verify the claim, and process it. As per IRDAI rules, standard claims must be settled within 30 days.

questions.text: Non-Standard Claims in insurance refer to claims where:
options: An accident occurred due to using a non-standard machine
Claims were intimated after a long time
The insured may have committed a breach of conditions and warranty
Loss was caused by an Act of God
questions.explanation: Non-Standard Claims are claims where the INSURED HAS BREACHED (violated) the conditions, warranties, or terms of the insurance policy. These claims take longer to process as the insurer conducts detailed surveys and investigations. Compensation may be reduced or denied.

questions.text: After the insurance company pays the claim for a damaged property, the SALVAGE (remains of the damaged property) belongs to:
questions.explanation: On payment of loss (claim), the SALVAGE belongs to the INSURER (insurance company). This follows the Principle of Subrogation — once compensation is paid, all rights over the damaged property transfer from the insured to the insurer. The insurer can then recover any residual value from the salvage.

questions.text: Arbitration in insurance claim disputes is governed by which Act?
questions.explanation: Arbitration in insurance claim disputes is governed by the ARBITRATION AND CONCILIATION ACT, 1996. In arbitration, an arbitrator is selected by MUTUAL CONSENT of both parties (insurer and insured) and helps resolve the dispute outside of court.

questions.text: Motor Third Party claims are settled through:
questions.explanation: MOTOR THIRD PARTY claims are exclusively settled through the MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL (MACT). This is a specialised legal body set up to handle motor accident third-party claims. They are NOT handled by civil courts, session courts, or internal insurance committees.

questions.text: In case of a FIRE CLAIM, the report from which authority is NECESSARY?
questions.explanation: For a FIRE CLAIM, the FIRE BRIGADE report is NECESSARY and mandatory. The fire brigade is typically the first authority to respond to a fire incident, and their report is the most reliable record of the cause, extent, and circumstances of the fire.

questions.text: For PERSONAL ACCIDENT CLAIMS, the report of which professional is mandatory?
questions.explanation: For PERSONAL ACCIDENT CLAIMS, the DOCTOR's report is mandatory. When a personal accident occurs, the first and most important step is medical treatment, and the doctor's medical report is the essential document to substantiate the nature and extent of the injury.

questions.text: Claims involving THIRD PARTY PROPERTY DAMAGE are assessed on the basis of:
options: Declaration of Owner of the Property
questions.explanation: Claims involving THIRD PARTY PROPERTY DAMAGE are assessed on the basis of the SURVEY REPORT prepared by the licensed and qualified surveyor who physically inspects and evaluates the damage.

questions.text: In HIT AND RUN cases where the vehicle causing the accident cannot be traced, claims are settled from:
questions.explanation: In HIT AND RUN cases where the offending vehicle cannot be identified, claims (for death or disability) are settled from the SOLATIUM FUND under the Solatium Scheme, 1989. This fund provides consolation compensation to victims even when no insurance policy can be traced.

questions.text: When should the intimation of loss be made to the insurance company?
options: At the exact time of the loss
questions.explanation: The intimation of loss to the insurance company should be made AS SOON AS REASONABLY POSSIBLE after the loss occurs. Early notification enables faster surveys and claim processing. Delayed intimation can complicate or jeopardise the claim.

questions.text: If an insurer settles a claim quickly and efficiently, what is the most significant outcome?
options: Insurer will be tempted to receive more claims
This will be the best advertisement for the insurer
Insurer will go into financial loss
Only habitual claimants will take insurance
questions.explanation: Quick and efficient claim settlement is the BEST ADVERTISEMENT for an insurance company. It demonstrates the insurer's commitment and capability to honour their promises. Good claim experience builds trust and attracts new policyholders through word of mouth.

questions.text: Which of the following activities would NOT be categorised as part of PROFESSIONAL claim settlement?
options: Seeking information about the cause of the loss
Approaching the claim with prejudice and bias
Checking whether the loss is covered under the policy
Quantifying the amount payable under the claim
questions.explanation: Approaching a claim WITH PREJUDICE or bias is NOT part of professional claim settlement. Professional settlement involves: objectively gathering cause-of-loss information, verifying coverage, and calculating the payable amount. Any approach based on prejudice, revenge, or malice is unprofessional and unethical.

questions.text: For Travel Insurance policies, claims arising OUTSIDE India are assessed by:
options: Local surveyors in the country of loss
Claims Settling Agent named in the policy
questions.explanation: For travel insurance claims arising outside India, the assessment is done by the CLAIMS SETTLING AGENT NAMED IN THE POLICY. The policy document specifically designates an agent (or claims handling company) in the destination country to handle overseas claims efficiently.

questions.text: As per the Insurance Act, an INDEPENDENT SURVEYOR is required when the value of a claim exceeds:
questions.explanation: As per the Insurance Act, an INDEPENDENT LICENSED AND QUALIFIED SURVEYOR is required when the claim value EXCEEDS Rs. 20,000. Below this threshold, the insurer's internal staff can handle the survey. (Note: IRDAI has proposed revising this limit, but for the current IRDAI IC-38 exam, Rs. 20,000 is the correct answer.)

questions.text: Loss investigation in insurance claims must be conducted by:
options: Any person holding an Engineering degree
questions.explanation: Loss investigation in insurance claims must be conducted by a LICENSED AND QUALIFIED SURVEYOR. Only a surveyor who holds a valid licence and the required qualifications is authorised to conduct official loss assessments. An unlicensed person, the insured's own representative, or an engineering graduate without a surveyor's licence cannot conduct the official investigation.
